steps.why: The review page's own gate region, with the run's artifact review still open and nothing decided.

cells.requires: SECTION IV of the ratified drawing at the contract's pin, verbatim: 'Four drawn states, and one that draws nothing.' 'A card is loading while the host prepares the target; restricted when the reader may see the gate but not decide it — the terminal affordances disabled, the reason shown; and no longer open when the gate was already settled or the run moved on, offering a refresh rather than letting a stale decision through.' 'Restricted is a card that renders: the reader sees the target and the disabled floor, with the reason on screen. Absent is no card DOM at all.' With SECTION II's floor, verbatim: 'The review card fills the assistant's turn: the target panel naming what is under review and pinning its exact revision, then the decision floor that governs it.' And app-artifact-review SECTION VI, verbatim: 'A single decision bar sits at the foot of the gate, governing every target under it. It offers exactly three affordances: Approve (primary), Reject (destructive), and Comment.' 'Approve and Reject are terminal — they resolve the gate and hand the run its outcome.' app-artifact-review SECTION I, verbatim: 'An agent run opens at its own canonical route under /agents. The surface is a two-column frame: a step rail down the left names the run's ordered steps, and the run detail on the right shows the selected step.' 'A resolved gate stays on the rail as read-only history — its entry keeps its place and records how it was settled (approved, rejected, changes requested), so the rail is the run's whole lifecycle at a glance, not just its live tip.' 'a gate step opens the gate's own surface in place — a pending review renders the review gate (SECTION III-SECTION VII) right here in the run detail, under the same rail, never as a standalone document.'

steps.why: The conversation the run was started from, after a change request was typed into the review's own prompt window and the repair returned.

cells.requires: SECTION VII of the ratified drawing at the contract's pin, verbatim: 'After a repair, the turn may carry a verification card: the Core analysis heading with its outcome pill, the scope sentence, the two revision pins, and the field-by-field before / after of exactly what was inspected. It carries no floor at all — it asks nothing, so it draws nothing to press. It closes with Advisory comments: a label over one panel per comment, each carrying its author kind in mono above the comment itself.' 'Three outcomes. Verified, Out-of-scope drift — a field changed that the review never covered, marked in place in the table — and Findings not met. The outcome pill is the only place the card carries state colour.'
